previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG, diabetes, hypertension, and asthma was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and productive cough over one week, associated with pleuritic chest pain and recent high salt intake. Evaluation revealed no evidence of pneumonia, pulmonary embolism, or acute myocardial infarction. Her symptoms were attributed to an acute exacerbation of diastolic heart failure, likely precipitated by dietary salt overload, along with acute bronchitis. She was treated with intravenous furosemide, which improved her respiratory status, and continued on her baseline cardiac, pulmonary, and diabetes medications. Her blood glucose improved with insulin therapy, and she was discharged home in stable condition with no medication changes and instructions to follow up with primary care and cardiology.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with a history of CAD s/p CABG ___, IDDM ___ HgA1c 
12.5%), HTN, HL ___ LDL 199) who presented with complaints of 
chest and back pain.
.
# Chest pain: Her pain was reproducible on palpation and did not 
respond to nitroglycerin. Because of her significant cardiac 
history she was ruled out for ACS with an unchanged EKG and 
normal cardiac enzymes. She then underwent a cardiac perfusion 
study which showed a normal cardiac perfusion and ejection 
fraction without evidence of ischemia. The pain is very likely 
musculoskeletal. She was started on percocet which wasa very 
effective at controlling her pain.

# Diabetes Mellitus: She is prescribed lantus 40 mg BID and 
humalog 10 mg TID with meals and metformin. However she 
initially reported that she was only taking her lantus once. 
When she was admitted her metformin was held because of the 
recent contrast study and mild creatinine elevation. Her blood 
sugar was >400 on multiple readings. We contacted her PCP who 
stated that she was supposed to be taking lantus 40 mg BID 
instead of daily but she later reported very infrequently taking 
her night dose of Lantus. When she received her BID dosing her 
blood sugar dropped into the ___ and she was symptomatic. ___ 
was consulted to simplify her home regimen and they recommended 
continuing her morning lantus, TID humalog and metformin but 
stopping the night dose. She was also instructed to keep a log 
of her blood sugars and discuss increasing her morning lantus 
dose with her primary doctor. Reassuringly, her hemoglobin A1c 
was 8.5 on this admission which has significantly improved from 
12.5 last time it was checked indicating that she is making 
significant progress in the long term management of her 
diabetes.
.
# Hypertension: She presented with SBP 200. She says that she 
did not take her blood pressure medicines prior to coming to the 
hospital. We restarted her home medications and her blood 
pressure was better controlled but her sytstolic BP still ranged 
in 130-160 range. We considered increasing her medications but 
decided that because of her poor medication compliance that we 
preferred not to make too many changes at once. She may  need 
blood pressure medication modifications if her blood pressure 
remains elevated. She was continued on metoprolol, lisinopril, 
imdur amlodipine and aspirin.
.
___: Creatinine elevated to 1.3 on presentation which is 
slightly above her baseline but she does have frequent variation 
in her baseline. This was felt to be from mild prerenal azotemia 
from osmotic diuresis from her hyperglycemia as well as mild 
diarrhea on presentation. Her weight on admssion was 143lbs 
which is down from her prior weights 145-148. She received 
gently hydration given her diastolic heart failure and her 
creatinine was 1.2 on discharge.
.
#CAD: She has a history of an inferior MI, CABG. She was ruled 
out for cardiac causes of her chest pain as above. She was 
continued on metoprolol, lisinopril, imdur amlodipine, 
atorvastatin and aspirin.
